newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Philippine President Fidel Ramos says he approved all real estate transactions entered into by the Public Estates Authority including the sale of a prime reclaimed property to Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp where the government allegedly lost up to 120 billion pesos. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- A group called the People's Initiative for Reform, Modernization and Action (Pirma) says it will launch a campaign to change the Constitution to allow President Ramos to seek re-election. (MANILA TIMES)
- Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi protests against her confinement at home by the military government, labelling the move as illegal. (TODAY)
- President Ramos issues Executive Order 381 creating a top level committee and working group on food security. (BULLETIN)
- Philippine merchandise exports grew by 17.6 percent to $1.883 billion from its year-ago level of $1.602 billion, the National Statistics Office said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Several publicly-listed companies have asked the Securities and Exchange Commission to defer the implementation of full disclosure rules on proxies to enable them to amend their corporate by-laws so they can comply with the new requirements. (MANILA TIMES)

- The Central Bank is opposing the planned withdrawal of some 36.1 billion pesos in national government deposits from the Central Bank's vaults, saying this would disrupt the carefully calibrated inflation targets in the remaining days of the year. (JOURNAL)

- The Department of Transportation and Communications says it will award the $500 million Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) terminal 3 project to the consortium of People's Air Cargo and Warehousing Co Inc. (BULLETIN)
- The National Economic and Development Authority says it will not revise annual inflation target of 8.7 percent even if oil prices continue to increase. (BUSINESSWORLD)
